title: Almighty God! Thy Wondrous Works
description: Almighty God! Thy Wondrous Works in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Beddome wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 139 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Mysteries of Providence”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Al-might-y God! thy won-drous works Of prov-i-dence and grace, An an-gel's per-fect mind ex-ceed, And all our pride a-base.

lines: Or, if a transient glimpse we gain,
Though all the mysteries lie concealed
Grant us the knowledge of ourselves,

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Beddome died in 1795.
credits: Words by Benjamin Beddome (1717–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
